question: Should the macOS entitlement-aware fallback preserve readable existing App Group identities before switching unentitled builds to legacy storage, or is a one-time identity reset acceptable?
rationale: This is a persisted auth/session identity choice: the patch fixes repeated churn for the canonical bug, but the new storage priority can intentionally change an existing user's device identity during upgrade.

options.title: Require Upgrade Preservation
options.body: Have the PR preserve or migrate a valid readable App Group identity into the chosen legacy store before falling back, with focused upgrade tests and signed-mac proof.

options.title: Accept One-Time Re-Pair
options.body: Maintainers may intentionally accept a one-time identity change for affected unentitled macOS installs, but that should be explicit in review and release notes.

options.title: Use App Groups Instead
options.body: Pause this fallback PR if the intended product direction is to sign and provision the macOS bundle with the App Groups entitlement.

recommendation.title: Require Upgrade Preservation
recommendation.body: Have the PR preserve or migrate a valid readable App Group identity into the chosen legacy store before falling back, with focused upgrade tests and signed-mac proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history ties steipete to both macOS local Gateway identity behavior and the macOS signing surface involved in this decision.
